Euclidean distance for Pb isotope ratios to ore sources

Source: R/ASTR_PbIso_Prov.R
pb_iso_prov_dist.Rd

Calculates the Euclidean distance of each isotope sample to a reference data set and gives the closest regions to the groups. Mass fractionation follows the procedure outlined in Albarede et al. (2024).

Usage

pb_iso_prov_dist(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ASTR'
pb_iso_prov_dist(
  x,
  ref,
  ref_group,
  dist_type = c("ed", "mf", "all"),
  n = 1,
  s = 0.001,
  ...
)

euc_dist(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ASTR'
euc_dist(x, ref, ref_group, n = 1, ...)

mf_dist(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ASTR'
mf_dist(x, ref, ref_group, n = 1, s = 0.001, ...)

Arguments

x

ASTR object containing 206Pb/204Pb, 207Pb/204Pb, 208Pb/204Pb isotope ratios for analysis.

...

Additional parameters.

ref

ASTR object containing 206Pb/204Pb, 207Pb/204Pb, 208Pb/204Pb isotope ratios as a provenance reference.

ref_group

Name of the column containing isotope groups as a character string.

dist_type

Distance type to use, simple Euclidean ("ed"), mass-fractionation corrected ("mfd"), or both ("all")

n

Length of result output, default value is 1.

s

Mass fractionation factor, default value is 0.001.

Value

ASTR object of matched x, reference, and corresponding distance values.

References

Albarede, F., Davis, G., Blichert-Toft, J., Gentelli, L., Gitler, H., Pinto, M., and Telouk, P. (2024) A new algorithm for using Pb isotopes to determine the provenance of bullion in ancient Greek coinage. Journal of Archaeological Science 163, 105919. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jas.2023.105919

See also

Other Pb isotope functions: age_models, as_pbiso_ref_data(), geom_sk_lines(), pb_iso_endmembers(), pb_iso_prov_predict(), pb_iso_train_data(), tel_dor

Examples

GlobaLID_ASTR_ref <- as_pbiso_ref_data(GlobaLID_ASTR,
                                   names(GlobaLID_ASTR)[[2]],
                                   min_groupsize = 5)

# Euclidean distance
euc_dist(tel_dor, GlobaLID_ASTR_ref, n = 1)

mf_dist(tel_dor, GlobaLID_ASTR_ref, n = 1, s = 0.001)
